name: Alert Engine Heartbeat
description: Liveness beacon written by the alert engine. Two independent clocks: last_seen (ANY beat — the engine's self-timer proves the process is alive) and last_ingest_at (an ingest-driven beat — proves telemetry is still arriving from Airflow). The monitor_alert_engine scheduled task emails ops when either goes stale, and names which one — 'engine down' and 'telemetry stopped' are different outages with different fixes.

fields.label: Last Seen (any beat)
fields.description: Server time the last heartbeat of ANY kind arrived. Stale => the engine process itself is down.

fields.label: Last Ingest Cycle
fields.description: Last beat posted from an /ingest cycle. Stale while last_seen is fresh => the engine is UP but Airflow has stopped delivering telemetry.

fields.label: Last Self-Timed Beat
fields.description: Last beat from the engine's own timer (engine >= 0.9.6). Set => this engine reports liveness independently of ingest, so the watchdog can separate the two failures.

fields.label: Last Beat Source
fields.description: ingest | timer — which kind of beat arrived last.

fields.label: Rules Loaded
fields.description: 0 => the engine has no config (nothing can fire).

fields.label: Last Alert Fired At
fields.description: Last cycle that actually fired an alert (fired > 0).

fields.label: Last Engine Error
fields.description: The most recent failure the engine itself reported, with its traceback. Included verbatim in the watchdog email so a page carries the stack trace instead of just 'something is wrong'.

fields.label: Error Context
fields.description: What the engine was doing (e.g. 'novu trigger 16:overspeed').

fields.label: Down Alert Sent
fields.description: Set when a 'down' email has been sent; cleared on recovery. Prevents email spam.

fields.label: Consecutive Bad Checks
fields.description: How many watchdog runs in a row saw a problem. Debounce: page only after alert_watchdog_confirm_checks consecutive bad runs, so a brief ingest gap / spot reschedule doesn't flap.
